function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Here are a few ways you can order a cake, depending on whether you’re looking for something local or something that can be delivered right to your door: | Option | What it offers | How to order | |--------|----------------|--------------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for special occasions | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp, call the bakery, or visit their website. Many bakeries now accept online orders via their own site or through platforms like **Etsy** (for custom designs). | | **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide delivery, wide variety of flavors & designs, some offer same‑day delivery in major cities | • **Goldbelly** – delivers specialty cakes from famous bakeries across the U.S.
• **Cake Delivery** – local delivery in many U.S. cities.
• **Amazon Fresh** – offers cakes from local vendors in select areas.
• **Instacart** – you can add a cake to your grocery list and have it delivered. | | **Specialty cake makers** | Custom designs, themed cakes, vegan or gluten‑free options | • **Etsy** – search “custom cake” and filter by location or shipping.
• **The Cake Shop** – a boutique that ships nationwide.
• **Local artisan bakers** – many have Instagram pages where you can DM to place an order. | | **Convenience stores / supermarkets** | Ready‑made cakes, quick pick‑up | • **Walmart** – has a bakery section in many stores.
• **Target** – offers a selection of cakes in the bakery aisle.
• **Whole Foods** – has a bakery with a variety of options. | | **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries (great for recurring celebrations) | • **Cratejoy** – look for “cake subscription” boxes.
• **Baker’s Box** – delivers a fresh cake each month. | ### Quick steps to place an order 1. **Decide on the occasion** (birthday, wedding, corporate event, etc.) and the size you need. 2. **Choose a flavor & design** – most sites let you upload a photo or choose from templates. 3. **Check delivery options** – same‑day, next‑day, or scheduled delivery. Make sure the delivery window fits your event. 4. **Place the order** – either through the bakery’s website, a third‑party platform, or by phone. 5. **Confirm details** – double‑check the address, delivery time, and any special instructions (e.g., “no frosting on top” or “vegan only”). If you tell me your city or zip code, I can narrow down the best local options for you!
